solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keep shortened shape with hair

indicators.note: something shortened has been cut, so the word for shape loses its final letter

blocks.note: form is the outline or shape of a thing
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a shortened shape to their hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: the strongest tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, so the noun is a synonym for a stronghold.

clue.text: Father has beer with no head and fried food

indicators.note: no head means the first letter of the drink is removed

blocks.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
bitter is a British style of beer

explanation.surface: Father has a pint without a frothy head alongside his fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: A head on beer is its froth, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritter is a piece of fruit, vegetable or meat coated in batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Madness having north in the middle for compass

indicators.note: in the middle places the abbreviation inside the word for madness

blocks.note: rage is a fit of madness
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Losing one's north on a compass would be maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: North and compass suggest navigation, but compass means scope here.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean scope or extent, as in within the compass of a study, a synonym for breadth.

clue.text: Go over a picture needing editing after office hours perhaps

indicators.note: editing changes the order of material, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
time after office hours is late; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A photograph needs editing after the office has closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is not a placement signal here; it belongs to the phrase that gives LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapitulate is to summarise or restate the main points, which is to go over them again.

clue.text: Dance with Samuel with ball only half completed

indicators.note: only half completed means just the first half of the word survives

blocks.note: Sam is a short form of Samuel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Samuel dances at a ball he only half finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance, especially associated with carnival in Rio.

clue.text: Time in charge for charity event

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other piece here

blocks.note: a fee is a charge for a service
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone is put in charge of the timing for a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a phrase meaning responsible, but it splits: T goes in FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising gathering with stalls and games, typically held for a church or good cause.

clue.text: Reserve ship supporting energy weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means holding up from below, so the vessel goes underneath

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
an arm is a weapon
Noah's Ark was a ship

explanation.surface: A ship's stores of energy and weapons are held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts ARK below E and ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to set aside funds or items for a particular purpose, keeping them in reserve.

clue.text: Admission of guard losing seconds

indicators.note: losing means the guard word drops the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A guard lets someone in within seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry is the act of going in or being allowed in, so it means admission to a place.

clue.text: Free of trouble on top of fell

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means sitting above, so the trouble word comes first

blocks.note: unrest is disturbance or trouble
rain fell, so it rained

explanation.surface: Someone is free of trouble at the top of a fell, a northern English hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like a hill, the surface sense, but it is the past tense of fall, describing rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means not held back or controlled, which is to be free of restriction.

clue.text: Style of column — one round and mostly attractive

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the adjective is dropped

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape
nice means pleasant or attractive

explanation.surface: A column is described as single, rounded and fairly attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, recognised by the scroll-shaped capitals on its pillars.

clue.text: Got together with Indian queen over inside tower

indicators.note: in an across clue, over suggests turning things back to front
inside tells us the Indian royal sits within the other word

blocks.note: people who got together met
a rani is the wife of a rajah or a ruling Indian queen

explanation.surface: People met up with an Indian queen inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian queen is turned around first, then placed inside the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender spire of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made, a kind of tower.

clue.text: Support the gutted English

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: the word the with its middle removed
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The English are gutted, perhaps after a sporting defeat, and need support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, but here it simply strips the inside of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is the small peg on which a golf ball is supported before being struck.

clue.text: Catch a Romeo during play dwelling on a heavenly body?

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so these pieces go within the drama word

blocks.note: taken as written
to net is to catch
taken as written
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo is caught out during a play while brooding over a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwelling on' looks like brooding about something, but the definition reads it as living on a planet; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetary means relating to or belonging to a planet, so a being living on one could be called planetary.

clue.text: After run I try a strange and uncommon thing

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
these three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: After a run, someone tries something strange and unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After run' puts R before the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something seldom found or seen, a rare and unusual object or occurrence.

clue.text: Military construction engineers provided with misgivings

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a doubt is a misgiving

explanation.surface: Army engineers have misgivings about a structure they are building.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification or outwork built to defend soldiers, a kind of military earthwork.

clue.text: Good man Joker — not the first one getting you heated?

indicators.note: not the first tells us the opening letter of the setter's name is removed

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
the setter's own pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter calls himself a good man, but one who winds solvers up.
explanation.walkthrough: Joker is the name of this puzzle's setter, so the clue jokes about him annoying the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker feeds fuel into a furnace or boiler, so the worker is literally the one making things hot.

clue.text: Wind instrument missing its second note — make a new arrangement

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the instrument word

blocks.note: the recorder is a simple woodwind instrument
of the letters in the instrument's name that are musical notes, E comes first and C second

explanation.surface: A recorder player misses a note and has to rearrange the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to put items into a different sequence, giving them a fresh arrangement.

clue.text: Area united in arrangement of Saladin is region once ruled by Moors

indicators.note: an arrangement here is a new ordering, so the name's letters are mixed up
in places the abbreviation for united among the letters of the name

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
the name taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Saladin unites an area, fitting for the Muslim sultan who fought the Crusaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia, in southern Spain, was the heart of al-Andalus, the Moorish kingdom that ruled Iberia for centuries.

clue.text: A doctorate written about one insect pest

indicators.note: written about means wrapped around, so the qualification encloses the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
a PhD is a doctorate degree
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctoral thesis is written about one insect pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' sounds like the subject of a thesis, but it means wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are small sap-sucking insects, such as greenfly, that damage garden plants and crops.

clue.text: Small border plant

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A small border plant, as in a garden flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border plant' reads as a garden term, but border gives EDGE and plant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant with triangular stems that grows in wet ground and marshes.

clue.text: Shout of disapproval from volume being reduced

indicators.note: something being reduced is made smaller, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A shout of disapproval greets the volume of a noise being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests loudness, which fits a shout, but here it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is the noise an audience makes to jeer or show dislike of a performer.

clue.text: Wash black articles

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Washing black items of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests clothing, but it means the grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash oneself or something by immersing it in water.

clue.text: Obsessed with Aunt Edwina’s shows

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the letters are on view inside the phrase

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with the TV shows their Aunt Edwina watches.
explanation.definitionFit: To be haunted by something is to be troubled or preoccupied by it, constantly returning to it in thought.

clue.text: Distinguished? Not the person who oversees these puzzles

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: the person who oversees these puzzles
blocks.note: the crossword editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A distinguished figure, but not the crossword editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter teases that the puzzle editor is not distinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means famous or well known, an adjective for a distinguished and eminent person.

clue.text: Information? A small amount gets sent back

indicators.note: something sent back returns to where it started, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone asks for information and gets only a little of it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for study, so the plural noun means gathered information.

clue.text: Kit put on top of school cap?

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the kit word follows the school word

blocks.note: the head is the person at the top of a school
gear is equipment or kit

explanation.surface: A school uniform kit topped off with a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of school' is the headteacher, not the first letter of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is anything worn on the head, and a cap is one example, hence the question mark.
